title.narrative: Skills for Industry Competitiveness and Innovation Program

description.narrative: The results-based program (RBL) will increase the provision of skilled workforce for industry competitiveness and innovation. The program will have the following outputs: (i) training for advanced technical skills in priority and emerging sectors improved, (ii) managerial capabilities and green innovation capacity strengthened, (iii) socially inclusive skilling and upskilling expanded, and (iv) institutional capacity for skills monitoring and management enhanced.

description.narrative: Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: Capacity for advanced technical skills training developed for emerging and priority sectors Indicator: At least 20 advanced technical courses implemented based on industry demands, including at least 3 courses specifically targeted for women (2023 baseline: Not applicable) (OP 3.2.2) Progress/Status: Training in 18 advanced courses has commenced. 7 in BITAC, 4 in BUFT, 4 in ILET and 3 in BRAC (ICT). Data Source: Semiannual progress reports, TMS reports Actual value:

Output: Capacity for advanced technical skills training developed for emerging and priority sectors Indicator: At least 3 international partnerships established for advanced technical courses (2023 baseline: Not applicable) (OP 7.3.3) Progress/Status: 3 MOUs for advanced training in the textile, automotive and light engineering sectors have been signed till date, as follows: (i) MOU among SICIP, MOTJ, and KOTERI; (ii) MOU among SICIP, DTE, and HRI; (iii) MOU among SICIP, BITAC and KoreaTech
Data Source: Semiannual progress reports, TMS reports Actual value:

Output: Capacity for advanced technical skills training developed for emerging and priority sectors Indicator: At least 35 practical training labs or workshops in advanced technologies created and operational for training (e.g., BUFT, STTLs, BITAC, polytechnics), including green technologies (2023 baseline: Not applicable) (DLI 4) (OP 3.1.3; 3.2.5) Progress/Status: 6 practical training labs for advanced light engineering in BITAC are already operational. Construction of STTL lab in Chittagong textile engineering college has begun. Construction of labs in Narsingdi Automotive Training Institute has begun. Data Source: Semiannual progress reports, TMS reports Actual value:

Output: Capacity for advanced technical skills training developed for emerging and priority sectors Indicator: At least 4,800 people (at least 15% women) enrolled in industry-demanded advanced or emerging technology courses (2023 baseline: Not applicable) (DLI 3) (OP 1.1.1; 2.1.1; 2.2.1) Progress/Status: 1,709 trainees (251 female; 15%) have enrolled in advanced technical courses on light engineering and fashion and garments. Data Source: Semiannual progress reports, TMS reports Actual value:

Output: Access to socially inclusive skilling and upskilling expanded Indicator: At least 18,000 people enrolled in international certificate courses for potential migrant workers (2023 baseline: 5 courses under SEIP) (DLI 8) (OP 1.1.1) Progress/Status: 313 people (36 female) have completed internationally certified training at Asia Technical Training Institute for TÜV SÜD certification, at BMET for City & Guilds certification, and AEOSIB for Bureau Veritas certification.
Contract for additional courses with certification by Bureau Veritas (with BEIOA) is under preparation. Data Source: Semiannual progress reports, TMS reports Actual value:

Output: Capacity for advanced technical skills training developed for emerging and priority sectors Indicator: At least 5 industry-academic partnerships established for advanced skills programs (2023 baseline: Not applicable) Progress/Status: 2 industry-academic partnerships have been signed. An MOU between SICIP and the Fair Group was signed on 31 December 2024 to support the development of skilled workforce for the emerging automobile industry. An MOU among SICIP, BUFT and Shin Shin Group was signed on 30 December 2024 to support training in advanced fashion and garments technology. Data Source: Semiannual progress reports, TMS reports Actual value:

Output: Institutional capacity for skills monitoring and management enhanced Indicator: Two rounds of performance audits of the RBL program (including implementing partners) undertaken and action plans implemented (2023 baseline: Not applicable) (DLI 9) Progress/Status: The first round of performance audits covering 24 implementing partners is ongoing. Draft report has been submitted on 30 June 2026. Data Source: Semiannual progress reports, TMS reports, and annual audit reports Actual value:

Output: Managerial capabilities and green innovation capacity strengthened Indicator: At least 5 R&D project outcomes have been piloted or adopted by industries or government agencies, including those using green technologies or skills (2023 baseline: Not applicable) (OP 3.1.5) Progress/Status: 12 R&D grant proposals based on university-industry collaboration have been finalized and agreements signed. Call for second batch of EOIs for R&D grant proposals is under preparation. Data Source: Semiannual progress reports, TMS reports Actual value:

Output: Managerial capabilities and green innovation capacity strengthened Indicator: At least 7 R&D projects implemented for industry development through university-industry collaborations (2023 baseline: Not applicable) (DLI 6) Progress/Status: 12 R&D grant proposals based on university-industry collaboration have been selected and agreements signed. Data Source: Semiannual progress reports, TMS reports Actual value:

Output: Access to socially inclusive skilling and upskilling expanded Indicator: At least 23,000 women enrolled in women-targeted skills programs, including multi-skilling courses and green skills programs (2023 baseline: 1,000 BWCCI courses) (OP 2.1.1) Progress/Status: 5,770 women have enrolled training in specialized programs run by BWCCI, WEAB and BMET (women TTCs) and 3,497 have been certified. Training partnership agreement has been signed with WEAB. Data Source: Semiannual progress reports, TMS reports Actual value:

Output: Access to socially inclusive skilling and upskilling expanded Indicator: At least 12 performance (results)-based training contracts signed and implemented with industry and NGO partners, covering at least 9 priority and emerging sectors (2023 baseline: 12) (OP 1.2.2) Progress/Status: Achieved. Contracts for entry and mid-level technical training have been signed with 17 industry associations and NGO partners as follows. a. Bangladesh Knitwear Manufacturers and Exporters Association b. Bangladesh Association of Construction Industry c. Bureau of Manpower, Employment and Training (BMET), d. Directorate of Technical Education (DTE), e. Kumudini Welfare Trust f. Bangladesh Road Transport Corporation (BRTC) g. Association of Export Oriented Ship Building Industries of Bangladesh (AEOSIB) h. Bangladesh Engineering Industry Owner's Association (BEIOA) i. Bangladesh Garments Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA) j. Tourism and Hospitality Industry Skills Council (ISCT&H) k. Leathergoods and footwear Manufacturers and Exporters Association (LFMEAB) l. Real Estate and Housing Association of Bangladesh (REHAB) m. Bangladesh Bank Small and Medium Sized Enterprises - Special Program Department (BB-SME) n. Palli Karma-Sahayak Foundation (PKSF) o. Bangladesh Women Chamber of Commerce and Industry (BWCCI) p. Bangladesh Association of Construction Industry (BACI)
Data Source: Semiannual progress reports, TMS reports Actual value:

Output: Access to socially inclusive skilling and upskilling expanded Indicator: At least 160,000 people (at least 30% women) enrolled in competency-based job-ready basic and mid-level skills courses (2023 baseline: 197,000) (DLI 7) (OP 1.1.1; 2.1.1) placement 3 months after training Progress/Status: 70,174 people (21,847 female; 31%) have been enrolled in job-ready basic and mid-level technical skills training. Data Source: Semiannual progress reports, TMS reports Actual value:

Output: Managerial capabilities and green innovation capacity strengthened Indicator: at least 3,250 people (15% women) enrolled in mid-level managerial training at EDCs, covering at least 4 industry sectors (2023 baseline: 283) (DLI 5) (OP 1.1.1; 2.1.1; 2.3.1) Progress/Status: 2,363 trainees (535 female; 23%) have been enrolled in EDC courses at BIGM, BUTEX, BRAC, IBA and EWU. and Management (BIGM), out of that total 601 were certified (162 female, 27%) Data Source: Semiannual progress reports, TMS reports Actual value:

Output: Access to socially inclusive skilling and upskilling expanded Indicator: At least 10,000 people from socially disadvantaged groups (e.g., orphans, people with disabilities, transgender people, people from small ethnic communities) enrolled in targeted skills programs (2023 baseline: 600) (OP 1.1.1) Progress/Status: A contract was signed with PKSF for targeted training program for a total of 7,300 trainees from socially disadvantaged backgrounds. This includes 5 courses for persons with disabilities, 10 courses for ethnic minorities and 2 courses for third-gender trainees. 675 trainees (186 female) are enrolled. Data Source: Semiannual progress reports, TMS reports Actual value:

Output: Institutional capacity for skills monitoring and management enhanced Indicator: An annual internal audit plan established, and by 2028, internal audits conducted covering at least 10 implementing partners and action plans in place (2023 baseline: Not applicable) (DLI 9) Progress/Status: Internal audits have been undertaken for 10 training partners. They include 4 EDCs namely EWU, BRAC University, IBA-Dhaka University, BUTEX, and also BIGM. The other entities audited in 2025 were AEOSIB, BEIOA, BGMEA, REHAB and DTE (a public training provider).
